evaluation: Root audits final source/graph semantics, correct/incorrect/unknown transitions and each actual edit rejection under the unchanged active editor and selector. A mechanical rejection is not an extraction semantic failure. Do not broaden metadata, infer exclusive ownership from citation overlap, or silently change the factor to order-only to obtain a pass.
procedure: Fresh context for each of two edited-source constructions and four ordinary record reviews. Review variants keep source and predicate text identical and differ only in the target list. Each reviewer sees no variant label, references or other output. At most one existing local patch per reviewed record set, no second reviewer or semantic retry. Retain all failures and source-review misjudgments. Fresh edited graphs expose missing/retained actions without references. Inverse ADD restores original bytes and reuses original evidence; it is not another natural sample.
question: Close a complete bounded TSG review/patch cycle and test actual whole-policy deletion without forcing policy-dependent entities to persist.
reference: Controls preserve complete targets and owned relations. Wrong-target variants should reject the extra directory-creation/database-insertion recipient without losing the correct actor or ordering. Deleted lower instruction must not remain as a required lowering call merely because a helper is defined; deleted hashing instruction must not remain as a prescribed hash operation, hashed value or hash-before-insert policy. Other explicit source requirements remain. Source omission does not prove generated software lacks the protection.
